<!-- pr-reviewer: 2d5c371a50c10c411a3b13c329c1410aead9bdc5 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** The head is green, but it does not merge cleanly with current main.

Thanks for the careful roundoff work and the numeric reference chains. The tolerance is applied only to endpoints, and the test keeps kind, feed, axis and move count strict. The 1e-6 clearance case proves real motion survives.

### What looks good
- `rapid()` in `crates/motion/src/drilling/cross.rs` snaps only targets within 1e-9 mm of the tip, and still calls `PathBuilder::push`, so pose changes are kept.
- `cross_invariance` covers the next_up(10) case and real clearance motion.
- The reference chains in `crates/app/tests/cross_chain_reference/mod.rs` are ordered and exact on everything except endpoints.
- No `unwrap`, `expect` or `panic` is added in source.

### Local results
**Blocking: the trial merge with current main conflicts in code.** `crates/motion/src/drilling/cross.rs` lines 195-201 and 288-294: main changed `traverse_s` to take `&CrossHole` (`traverse_s(&hs[i - 1], h, hop_s)`), while this PR calls it with `.dir` and wraps the rapids in `rapid()`. The head was integrated with c9a9fb3, which is no longer main. Per the review rules I did not merge; I reviewed the head as is.

Head results, unmerged (based on c9a9fb3):

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | built, exit 0 |
| app `drilling_cross_box` | 7 passed |
| app `drilling_cross_spindle` | 7 passed |
| motion `cross_invariance` | 2 passed |
| motion lib `drilling` | 34 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | exit 0 |

### Requested before merge
1. Run `git merge origin/main` on `issue/151-cross-drill-invariance`, resolve `cross.rs` (keep main's `traverse_s(&hs[i - 1], h, hop_s)` signature and wrap its rapids in `rapid(&mut b, ...)`), re-run `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_spindle` and `cross_invariance`, and push.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
1. `RECOMMENDED.md` conflicts with main as well. That is a ledger file, so it is not blocking; the maintainer will move the entry to `docs/decisions` when it merges.
2. The release note says `fix:` merges once reviewed, and the commit body ends `Fixes #151`, so the issue closes on merge. Thanks for the complete gate receipts in the body.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

<!-- pr-reviewer: d0bb8d2d027e0f62c2919412817a7cdbac49efe9 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge**

Thanks for the careful rework, @seelesturm.

**What looks good**
- `rapid()` (crates/motion/src/drilling/cross.rs:84) is local to cross-drill radial rapids: it snaps to the cursor only within 1e-9 mm, and still goes through `PathBuilder::push`, so stationary station-pose changes are kept. The shared CL builder is untouched.
- It composes with main's whole-hole `traverse_s` calls; no unwrap/expect/panic or unchecked casts are added, and the stock/holder/part safety proofs are unchanged.
- `crates/motion/tests/cross_invariance.rs` pins both sides: ULP-level radius noise adds no move, and a real 1e-6 mm clearance and the initial index pose are kept.
- Raw-float hashes are replaced by portable reference chains (tolerance on endpoints only).
- The decision lives in `docs/decisions/151-cross-drill-invariance.md`; `RECOMMENDED.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` are not touched. The body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #151`, commit subjects are conventional, and no dependencies, build.rs, scripts or workflows change.

**Local results (PR head merged with current origin/main; merged cleanly, no conflicts)**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --no-run` | ok |
| motion lib `drilling` | 34 passed |
| motion `cross_invariance` | 2 passed |
| app `drilling_cross_box` | 7 passed |
| app `drilling_cross_spindle` | 7 passed |
| app `drilling_cross_stock` | 8 passed |
| clippy motion + app, all targets, `-D warnings` | clean |

**Requested before merge**
None.

**Notes (not blocking)**
- `cross.rs` is exactly 400 lines; any further growth should split along a seam.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
